Abstract: In the space below, please provide a destríptive summary of your proposed research project.
The pathogenesis of heart failure is still only poorly understood. The transition from compensated hypertrophy
to failure is accompanied by a progressive apoptotic loss of cardiomyocytes. Interestingly, stimuli of
hypertrophy as well as apoptosis șhare the AP-I signaling complex as a central regulatory element. AP-1 is a
composite transcription factor, whose subunit composition and interaction with other transcription factors may
vary. It can be hypothesized that under conditions favoring cardiac growth or apoptosis the composition of the
AP-1 complex differs and, due to this difference, different AP-1 controlled pathways become activated.
Variations in AP-1 transcription complexes may trigger the transition from hypertrophy to apoptosis in the
myocardialcells.
It is the cenral aim of this project to identify on the cellular level the different compositions of AP-1 complexes
under hypertrophy and apoptosis inducing conditions. Isolated cardiomyocytes from adult rat are used as
model. The a-adrenoceptor agonist phenylephrine and the NO-donor SNAP will be used as examplatory stimuli
for induction of AP-1 mediated hypertrophy and apoptosis, respectively. The expression of AP-1 components,
of interacting transcription factors, of target genes controlled by these specific AP-1 complexes and AP-1
driven “doynstream” genes specific for one or the other kind of stimulus will be identified with suitable
molecular techniques. The causal roles of transcription factors and other genes will be tested with use of decoy
or antisense oligonucleotides. It will also be tested if adenoviral overexpression of identified pro-apoptotic AP-
1 components or dependent genes can transform hypertrophic stimuli into apoptotic processes or if pro-
hypertrophic genes protect the cells against apoptotic stimuli. Finally, the relevance of the results obtained in
the cellular model will be evaluated in an established in vivo model of cardiac hypertrophy and failure, i.e. the
SHR-sp rat. The expression of the previously identified transcription factors and other genes, related to
hypertrophy or apoptosis, will be analyzed in these rats at the stages of compensated hypertrophy, transition to
heart failure and at manifest failure. A provocation test performed on hearts isolated from these animals will
functionally demonstrate their rlative propensity for apoptosis.
In summary, the project is designed to analyze on the molecular level the role of AP-1 signaling as a central
switch for induction of hypertrophy or apoptosis and heart failure.
